### dilla/data/bed.yml

`````yaml
# The bed: the pad, the drums on top of it, the lead and the bass.
#
# module Bed in MASTER/tools/dilla/dilla.rb renders it and reads every number below;
# nothing else keeps a copy. A bare `ruby dilla.rb` plays the catalogue through
# it, and `ruby dilla.rb bed` plays it under MASTER's narration, which is where
# it began (MASTER/data/voice.yml points here). A key with no reader in module
# Bed is a defect, and MASTER/tools/test/test_dilla_bed.rb pins the decisions that are
# easiest to undo by accident.
# The chords are dilla's, and in a narration pass only the ones he actually played.
#
# CHORD_PROGRESSIONS has 242 entries and most are theory, which under speech
# sounds like an exercise. The verified rows are transcribed from records,
# and a row that is transcribed is played as written: no borrowed ii-V, no
# added sus, no m6 for m7, no #11 added to a major chord. Each of those
# rewrites a transcription, which is the one thing the table promises not
# to be. The harmonic rhythm is in the rows too, written as repetition --
# Dm7 Dm7 Ebm7 Dm7 is Miles's 16:8:8 -- so every chord gets the same length.
progressions: artist_verified
records: ["Slum Village - Fantastic Vol 2", "Jay Dee - Another Batch", "Flying Lotus - Los Angeles"]
bpm: 88
bars_per_chord: 2
chords_per_pass: 12
# Each pass is measured and set to the loudness
# target, so a pass of pads and a pass of kit arrive at one level, with a
# true-peak ceiling because a limiter on sample peaks still clips between
# them.
loudness: { lufs: -14.0, true_peak_db: -1.0 }
# The measured target. Nine octave bands, each relative to the sub, averaged
# over three minute-long slices of Fantastic Vol 2 (at 10, 30 and 50 min).
# `bed.rb --check` renders three seeded passes and compares.
reference: { file: "~/.claude/hooks/bed_renders/ref.wav", slices_s: [600, 1800, 3000], seconds: 60 }
reference_bands: [0.0, -0.4, -5.6, -13.3, -16.7, -18.8, -19.2, -16.9, -20.3]
band_tolerance_db: 3.0
# Voice leading: common tones held, the rest moved by the smallest step, the
# third and seventh inside one octave, the upper structure inside two, and
# the fifth dropped from any chord of five tones or more.
voicing: { bass_range: [33, 45], upper_range: [52, 84], max_span: 24, drop_fifth_from: 5 }
# Chords overlap like a sustain pedal: the next one enters whole on the bar
# line while the last one's tail fades under it.
crossfade_s: 0.35
oversample: 4
chop:
  orders: [[0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 0, 1], [0, 2, 1, 3], [0, 1, 3, 2], [3, 1, 2, 0]]
  reverse_odds: 0.12
# One instrument per progression. A band does not change keyboards every
# chord, and a phrase played on one instrument is heard as a phrase. Every
# family is the engine's own oscillators: dilla synthesises every sound it
# plays, and a soundfont is a recording of somebody else's instrument.
families:
  rhodes: { source: oscillator, struck: true }
  moog: { source: oscillator }
  prophet: { source: oscillator }
# Every chord goes through AnalogSynth in lib/sound.rb -- oscillator stacks
# with drift, a four-pole Moog ladder with real resonance, and separate
# amplitude and filter envelopes. The `wave`, `cutoff`, `res` and `attack`
# below describe the same instrument as an ffmpeg expression, which is what
# the bed built before 2026-09-16 and what it falls back to when
# synth_voices is off. An expression has no feedback, so its resonance was an
# equalizer bump standing in for a filter, and it had no envelope at all: the
# chord arrived at one brightness and stayed there. That is the whole reason
# the pads sounded like arithmetic.
synth_voices: true
# How far each voice sits from concert pitch, in cents, when the bed plays a
# chord. AnalogSynth seeds every note separately, so this is not one instrument
# drifting: at its own default of four cents two tones of a chord could sit
# eight apart, which does not read as analogue warmth, it reads as out of tune,
# and on a ninth chord it destroys the beating between the partials that is the
# point of the voicing. A line can have the four; a chord gets this.
voice_drift_cents: 0.7
# The oscillator presets. Detune stays inside five cents: past that a chord
# reads as out of tune rather than as chorus.
patches:
  - { name: rhodes mk1,      family: rhodes,  wave: fm_wood,  cutoff: 1400, res: 2.0, attack: 0.04, detune_cents: [0, 2.8], synth: rhodes_tine }
  - { name: rhodes suitcase, family: rhodes,  wave: fm_bell,  cutoff: 1500, res: 1.5, attack: 0.05, detune_cents: [0, 5.0, -5.0], synth: rhodes_tine }
  - { name: rhodes bark,     family: rhodes,  wave: fm_glass, cutoff: 1200, res: 3.5, attack: 0.03, detune_cents: [0, 1.6], synth: rhodes_tine }
  - { name: rhodes soft,     family: rhodes,  wave: sine,     cutoff: 1100, res: 1.0, attack: 0.09, detune_cents: [0, 3.8, -3.8], synth: rhodes_tine }
  - { name: moog bowed,      family: moog,    wave: saw,      cutoff: 900,  res: 5.5, attack: 1.4,  detune_cents: [0, 5.0, -4.8], synth: warm_pad }
  - { name: moog bassoon,    family: moog,    wave: square,   cutoff: 560,  res: 8.5, attack: 0.6,  detune_cents: [0, -4.8], synth: moog_bass }
  - { name: moog horn,       family: moog,    wave: saw,      cutoff: 780,  res: 6.5, attack: 1.1,  detune_cents: [0, 3.6, -3.3], synth: poly_strings }
  - { name: moog reed,       family: moog,    wave: pulse,    cutoff: 1050, res: 7.0, attack: 0.5,  detune_cents: [0, 5.0, -5.0], synth: soft_reed }
  - { name: prophet strings, family: prophet, wave: saw,      cutoff: 1050, res: 4.0, attack: 2.0,  detune_cents: [0, 5.0, -5.0, 0.8], synth: prophet_five }
  - { name: prophet pwm,     family: prophet, wave: pulse,    cutoff: 1300, res: 3.5, attack: 0.8,  detune_cents: [0, 5.0, -5.0, 1.7], synth: juno_pad }
  - { name: prophet brass,   family: prophet, wave: saw,      cutoff: 1450, res: 5.0, attack: 0.45, detune_cents: [0, 4.8, -4.5], synth: prophet_five }
  - { name: prophet choir,   family: prophet, wave: triangle, cutoff: 1200, res: 2.5, attack: 1.7,  detune_cents: [0, 5.0, -5.0, 0.2], synth: vp330_ensemble }
# A pad that is not struck never starts faster than this: a fast attack is
# an event, and an event draws the ear off the voice.
min_attack_s: 0.4
chord_level_db: -14
pad_racks: [wash, shimmer]
# The chord played as rhythm: each tone on its own sixteenth with a short decay,
# so the harmony arrives as a sequence of pitched hits rather than as a pad. Off
# by default -- a held chord is what a bed is for -- and the techno pieces turn
# it on, because there a sustained chord is the thing that makes the track stand
# still.
pad_stabs: { steps: [0, 3, 6, 10], hold_s: 0.14, odds: 0.0 }
# A space echo on the pads, and only that.
#
# The lead gets the whole drawn chain because it is sparse and a fold or a
# crusher on two seconds of line is character. The pads sound three quarters of
# every bar, and measured tonight it is exactly the folder, the crusher and the
# phaser that cost this mix its air and its width -- a phaser notches both
# channels the same way, which removes energy and collapses the picture at
# once. An echo does neither: it adds depth behind the chord and takes nothing
# off the top. So the draw is filtered to the two stages that give a place
# without charging for it, and the wet is half, because a pad is already wide.
# stages is the trim, and random_plan applies it before `only` is applied here:
# it drops the costliest first, keeps reverb, and the cheap survivors are the
# fold and the crusher, which are the two this excludes. Set to 2 it therefore
# drew reverb on its own. Left untrimmed, so the filter does the choosing.
# Off, on the measurement. At wet 0.5 it cost 1.1 of loudness range and 4.9 dB of
# upper-mid against the arrangement without it, and returned 1 dB of air: a pad
# sounds three quarters of every bar, so a room behind it softens the chord more
# than it places it. The lead can afford one because it is sparse. Raise the wet
# to hear it; the machinery and the filter stay.
pad_space: { stages: 7, wet: 0.5, only: [space_echo, reverb] }
# Which families deal_instruments draws from and which presets inside them.
# All of both here; a piece in data/pieces.yml narrows the list, and that
# narrowing is most of what makes one piece a Rhodes record and the next a
# Prophet one. An empty list means all of them, not none.
pad_families: [rhodes, moog, prophet]
pad_patches: []
# One AnalogSynth voice for the whole piece, named outright.
#
# pad_families narrows which family deals and deal_instruments then picks a
# preset inside it, which is right for a pass that moves through several
# progressions. A catalogue piece is one progression, so the draw gives it one
# instrument anyway -- and with four rhodes presets all pointing at rhodes_tine
# the draw was choosing between four names for the same sound. Naming the voice
# per piece is what makes the catalogue a catalogue rather than one instrument
# playing sixteen sets of changes. Null leaves the draw alone.
pad_voice:
# The harmonic series under the chord: sines at whole multiples of its lowest
# note. A whole multiple of a frequency is what being in tune means, so this
# can be poured on without leaving the key -- the difference between a chord
# that is sustained and one that is lush. Off in the bed itself, where speech
# sits on top and the midrange is spoken for; the ambient pieces run it at -15.
overtones: { partials: [], gain_db: -20 }
hocket_odds: 0.33
reverse_odds: 0.17
bag_depth: 3
lead:
  rhythm_from: bar_shape
  pitch_from: chord_bag
  plays_odds: 0.25
  gain_db: -7
  # Each rack's own trim, measured on the same dry bars through every rack, so
  # the rotation changes colour without jumping in level.
  racks: { tape: -2.2, weather: 1.9, octave: -2.1, inharmonic: 5.1, ring: -3.7, ghost: 1.0 }
  stack_odds: 0.12
  freeze_odds: 0.3
  freeze_grains: 12
  gate_odds: 0.25
  glide_ms: 35
  order_flip_odds: 0.3
  sit_out_bars: 8
  # Close harmony on the lead: the melody carried by several voices a chord tone
  # apart, below it, each entering a few milliseconds after the last. Voices of 1
  # is one singer. Four is a vocal group.
  stack: { voices: 4, entry_ms: 9, falloff_db: 2.2 }
  # The room the line plays in, drawn per pass rather than written down.
  #
  # SpaceFx (lib/sound.rb) picks from a wavefolder, a bit crusher, a phaser, a
  # chorus, a tremolo, a space echo with wow on its delay, and a reverb, then
  # sorts what it drew into the order those belong in: distortion before a
  # filter sounds like an instrument and after it sounds like a broken speaker,
  # and the room goes last because everything before it is the sound and the room
  # is where the sound happens. The reverb is always there and always last.
  #
  # The live path has drawn its chains this way since it was written and the bed
  # never has, which is why the bed's lead sat dry under a wet pad. `stages`
  # trims the draw: live needs the samples before the speaker wants them and a
  # render does not, so a render can afford all seven.
  # Heavy, and the echo is not optional. A drawn chain is a coin toss per stage,
  # which is right for variety and wrong when one stage IS the sound: a tape echo
  # and its wow are the character of this lead, not a garnish the draw may skip.
  # `always` puts it in whatever the coins did.
  space: { stages: 7, wet: 1.0, always: [space_echo, reverb] }
# The bass line under the bed: dilla's ImprovisedLine.bass, rendered as a
# rounded wave with a sine at its own pitch under it -- an octave lower lands
# below the kick, where nothing is heard and the sub band swells -- lowpassed so it is felt more than
# heard, and ducked under the kick so the kick keeps its attack.
# Deeper: more of the sine that sits under the wave, and four decibels more of
# all of it. Not an octave down -- that was tried and refused just above,
# because it lands beneath the kick where nothing is heard and only the sub
# band swells. Weight at the fundamental is body; an octave down is rumble.
bass: { wave: triangle, cutoff_hz: 340, decay: 1.3, gain_db: -5, sine_mix: 0.95 }
# A catalogue piece through the bed: a two-chord vamp is stated until the
# piece has four chords to move through, a long progression is cut at eight,
# and the pieces are joined with a crossfade into demo.wav.
catalogue: { min_chords: 4, max_chords: 8, crossfade_s: 1.0 }
sidechain:
  pads: { threshold: 0.055, ratio: 7, attack_ms: 4, release_ms: 190, makeup: 1.6 }
  lead: { threshold: 0.08, ratio: 4, attack_ms: 3, release_ms: 150, makeup: 1.2 }
  dust: { threshold: 0.04, ratio: 3, attack_ms: 2, release_ms: 120, makeup: 1.0 }
  bass: { threshold: 0.06, ratio: 3, attack_ms: 3, release_ms: 140, makeup: 1.0 }
# The bed moves for the speech. speaker.rb holds the flag while a line
# plays, and the player crossfades to a copy of the pass with the voice
# band carved out and the level down.
speech: { flag: "~/.claude/hooks/speaking", duck_db: -4, carve: { hz: 2800, octaves: 1.0, gain_db: -6 }, attack_ms: 120, release_ms: 700 }
# The bus, and the two compressors on it.
#
# They were -22 dB at 3.4:1 and -19 dB at 2.6:1, in series, after a soft clip
# and before a tanh stage, a crusher and a limiter -- and the pad path already
# carried a limiter of its own, a rack compressor and a sidechain before it
# arrived. Measured on one chord, the voice leaves AnalogSynth with 19.1 dB of
# crest and 19.2 LRA and reaches the finished mix at 1.4: the chain was
# flattening the instrument into a tone. Gentler now -- the limiter catches the
# peaks, which is its job, and the compressors shape rather than squash.
master_bus:
  drive: 1.25
  pre_clip_threshold: 0.9
  rumble_hz: 42
  body_hz: 100
  crush_bits: 14
  crush_mix: 0.18
  width: 1.08
  mono_below_hz: 120
  limit: 0.92
  console: none
  compressors:
    - { threshold_db: -16, ratio: 1.8, attack_ms: 28, release_ms: 240, makeup: 1.3 }
    - { threshold_db: -11, ratio: 1.4, attack_ms: 40, release_ms: 300, makeup: 1.1 }
# The console a bus may leave through. lib/livesets.rb writes Sonitex STX-1260
# and Nasty VCS as chains and measures both; these are the stacks, named, so a
# piece picks its colour with a word. One instance is a colour and three are a
# sound, which is why glue is three.
#
#   none        the bus as it was before a piece could ask for a console.
#   glue        the sets' master row: vcs, a 1260, vcs again.
#   twelve_bit  the sampler lineage, hard: 12 bits and a 7.6 kHz ceiling.
#   air         gentler, for something held -- the crush that reads as grit on
#               a stab reads as hiss on a pad. Its ceiling is 15 kHz:
#               at the sets' 9 kHz an ambient piece measured -34 dB at 8k and
#               -50 at 16k, which is not gentle, it is closed.
#   blown       the 1260 at full wet, half rate, driven a quarter harder.
# A console stage where each stem enters the sum, not only on the master.
#
# Nasty VCS is a summing colour: what a desk does is add things, and the reason
# summed material glues is that every channel went through the same iron on the
# way in. One instance is a colour and three are a sound, so the longest path
# here -- a stem, the sum, the master -- is three, which is the warm side of the
# line lib/livesets.rb measured. `none` for dust, because a record's surface is
# already the colour and a second 1260 only raises its noise floor.
stem_consoles:
  # Every stem through the console, by the operator's decision of 2026-09-16:
  # everything on. The measured cost is 3.7 to 4.6 dB across presence, bite,
  # air and top and about 6 dB of stereo width, because a phaser puts the same
  # notches in both channels and so removes energy and narrows the picture at
  # once. Written down so a later reader knows the trade was chosen rather than
  # overlooked; kit and bass alone is two words away.
  pads: vcs_warm
  lead: vcs_wide
  bass: vcs_tight
  kit: vcs_warm
  dust: vcs_tight

# The machine the sum goes to tape on, before the master's own console. The
# head bump is the low lift a tape head gives near 60 Hz, wow is the capstan's
# slow speed error and flutter its fast one, the rolloff is the top the tape
# cannot hold, and the drive is into a tanh, which is what tape saturation is.
tape:
  head_bump_hz: 58
  head_bump_db: 2.6
  drive: 1.35
  wow_hz: 0.28
  wow_depth: 0.0035
  flutter_hz: 5.7
  flutter_depth: 0.0018
  rolloff_hz: 19000
consoles:
  vcs_warm:
    - [vcs, { depth: 0.36, smear: 2.2 }]
  vcs_wide:
    - [vcs, { depth: 0.44, smear: 3.4 }]
  vcs_tight:
    - [vcs, { depth: 0.28, smear: 1.2 }]
  none: []
  glue:
    - [vcs, { depth: 0.34, smear: 2.4 }]
    - [sonitex, { bits: 10, lo: 46, hi: 11500, drive: 1.1 }]
    - [vcs, { depth: 0.26, smear: 3.6 }]
  twelve_bit:
    - [sonitex, { bits: 12, lo: 70, hi: 7600, drive: 1.22 }]
    - [vcs, { depth: 0.5, smear: 1.6 }]
  air:
    - [vcs, { depth: 0.3, smear: 4.4 }]
    - [sonitex, { bits: 13, lo: 42, hi: 15000, drive: 1.04 }]
  blown:
    - [sonitex, { bits: 8, lo: 60, hi: 6000, drive: 1.5, mix: 1.0, samples: 2 }]
    - [vcs, { depth: 0.6, smear: 1.2 }]
# Measured rather than chosen, and only part of each delta applied: a full
# correction chases the reference into its own arrangement, and this one
# has speech on top. It sits after the compressor, whose makeup gain would
# otherwise put a cut midrange straight back.
tilt:
  applied_fraction: 0.7
  position: after_compressor
  bells:
    - { hz: 85,    octaves: 1.0, gain_db: 5.5 }
    - { hz: 175,   octaves: 1.0, gain_db: 2.1 }
    - { hz: 350,   octaves: 1.2, gain_db: -1.1 }
    - { hz: 700,   octaves: 1.2, gain_db: 2.6 }
    - { hz: 1400,  octaves: 1.2, gain_db: 1.4 }
    - { hz: 2800,  octaves: 1.2, gain_db: -2.6 }
    - { hz: 5600,  octaves: 1.2, gain_db: -0.8 }
    - { hz: 11000, octaves: 1.2, gain_db: 4.5 }
# A synth is silent between the notes and a record never is. The crackle
# comes round every 1.8 s, which is one turn at 33 rpm, and it ducks under
# the kick the way a record's surface hides under a transient.
dust: { hiss_db: -30, crackle_db: -14, band_hz: [900, 7000], rotation_s: 1.8 }
drums:
  reference: dilla_time
  kit: karriem_riggins
  grids: samples/midi
  # Named from what the grids contain, not from what they are called.
  #
  # The techno bank globbed four_floor_soul, push_*, uk_skip, footwork_lite and
  # euclid_*, and of those thirteen shapes exactly one had a kick on 0,4,8,12.
  # The rest are euclidean and Afro-Cuban rhythms -- cinquillo, tresillo -- plus
  # footwork and UK skip: good material, and none of it techno. Since the
  # arrangement walks the pool a block at a time, twelve blocks in thirteen came
  # out with the kick off the floor, which is why the techno pieces did not sound
  # like techno. Surveyed across all 72 grids, nine are four to the floor and
  # they are named here outright.
  #
  # The broken bank keeps everything the techno one wrongly held, because those
  # patterns are worth having where a piece wants them.
  grid_banks:
    dilla: [dilla_*, head_nod, soul_shuffle, questlove_pocket, neo_busy, half_soul, gospel_pocket, jazz_brush]
    flylo: [flylo_*, knxwledge_haze, hiatus_broken, ghost_cloud, air_pocket, samba_pulse, afro_clave]
    techno: [four_floor_soul, industrial_techno, sp1200, sp303, sp_chop, boom_808]
    broken: [euclid_*, push_*, uk_skip, footwork_lite, dembow_lite, trap_half, broken_kick]
    industrial: [industrial_techno, sp1200, sp303, mpc3000, madlib_dusty, crate_dig, boom_*, pack_729_*]
  crate: samples/drums
  samples: { kick: kick.wav, snare: snare.wav, ghost: ghost.wav, hat: hat.wav, open_hat: open_hat.wav, clap: ind_clap.wav }
  # Dilla time: the hats rigid, the snare rushed, the kick swung and late,
  # the ghosts later still. The parts disagree, and the disagreement is the
  # groove. The engine's own `dilla_drag` feel (lib/groove.rb) drags the
  # snare late instead. They differ on purpose: this rushed snare is the feel
  # the operator heard and kept when the bed became the render (2026-09-14),
  # and the engine's other renders keep the drag he was given on 2026-09-08.
  # One drum-grid registry (restructuring proposal 9) settles it for both.
  feels:
    hat:   { swing: 0.0,  shift: 0.0,    drift: 0.0 }
    snare: { swing: 0.0,  shift: -0.014, drift: 0.002 }
    kick:  { swing: 0.17, shift: 0.016,  drift: 0.004 }
    ghost: { swing: 0.17, shift: 0.026,  drift: 0.004 }
  hat_accents: { downbeat: 0.95, eighth: 0.7, sixteenth: 0.45, jitter: 0.3, open_odds: 0.35 }
  tape: { head_bump_hz: 60, head_bump_db: 3.4, drive: 1.7, wow_hz: 0.31, flutter_hz: 6.2, rolloff_hz: 14000 }
  slam: { threshold_db: -38, ratio: 12, attack_ms: 0.6, release_ms: 90, makeup_db: 8, blend: 0.6 }
  finish: sonitex_sp1200
  sonitex: { drive: 1.45, bandwidth_hz: 8000, crush_bits: 12, crush_hz: 26095, crush_mix: 0.52, lowpass_hz: 12000 }
  gain_db: -8
  arrangement: { bars_per_shape: 8, bank_order: [dilla, flylo, dilla, techno, industrial] }
# demo.wav: one piece of about six minutes, read by module Composition in
# dilla.rb. A section shapes the parts and never removes the drums: it thins
# them (density is the odds a hit other than the kick plays), filters them,
# chooses their voices and may drop the kick for a bar or two. Two drum layers
# play under every bar: `kit` is the bed's grid kit in dilla time and `hate` is
# a DillaSemantics profile rendered at the bed's tempo, so the heavy section is
# the HATE layer pushed over a kit that keeps swinging. Gains are dB, -60 is
# silent, and each moves to its section's value over `ramp_bars`; a pair of
# cutoffs sweeps across the section. A kick dropout sits only where the HATE
# layer carries no kick of its own, or the dropout would not be heard.
composition:
  ramp_bars: 2
  fade_out_s: 6
  lead_every: 2
  # The motif's rhythm in sixteenths; its pitches are motif_from_chord's degrees
  # of the chord the lead enters on, played on whichever chord is sounding.
  motif: { steps: [0, 3, 6, 10], lengths: [3, 2, 4, 5], velocities: [0.9, 0.7, 0.8, 0.65] }
  # Percussion answers each lead note this many sixteenths later.
  answer: { steps: 2, velocity: 0.35 }
  transforms:
    humanize: { ms: 8, spread: 0.12 }
    swing: { amount: 0.54 }
    shift: { steps: 1 }
    stretch: { factor: 1.5 }
    reverse: {}
    repeat: { times: 2 }
    ratchet: { count: 3, odds: 0.25 }
    ghost: { odds: 0.3, level: 0.3 }
    accent: { amount: 1.25 }
    drop: { odds: 0.15 }
    transpose: { semitones: 12 }
    invert: {}
    chop: { pieces: 3 }
    stutter: { steps: 2, repeats: 4 }
    probabilize: { odds: 0.7 }
    quantize: { strength: 1.0 }
    resample: { rate: 0.75 }
  sections:
    - name: atmosphere
      bars: 11
      grid: dilla
      voices: [kick, hat]
      density: 0.4
      drums: [humanize]
      hate: { profile: basic_channel, elements: [perc_b, texture] }
      lead: []
      gains_db: { texture: -4, kit: -2, hate: -12, bass: -60, pads: -60, lead: -60 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [500, 900], hate: [2500, 2500], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: pulse
      bars: 11
      grid: dilla
      voices: [kick, ghost, hat]
      density: 0.55
      drums: [humanize]
      hate: { profile: basic_channel, elements: [perc_a, perc_b, texture] }
      lead: []
      gains_db: { texture: -3, kit: 0, hate: -12, bass: -60, pads: -60, lead: -60 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [1500, 4000], hate: [4000, 4000], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: bass
      bars: 11
      grid: dilla
      voices: [kick, snare, ghost, hat]
      density: 0.7
      drums: [humanize]
      hate: { profile: hardgroove, elements: [hat, perc_a, perc_b] }
      lead: []
      gains_db: { texture: -6, kit: 0, hate: -12, bass: 0, pads: -60, lead: -60 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [7000, 7000], hate: [6000, 6000], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: chords
      bars: 11
      grid: flylo
      voices: [kick, snare, ghost, hat, open_hat]
      density: 0.85
      drums: [humanize, swing]
      hate: { profile: hardgroove, elements: [hat, perc_a, perc_b] }
      lead: []
      gains_db: { texture: -8, kit: 0, hate: -12, bass: 0, pads: 0, lead: -60 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [12000, 12000], hate: [8000, 8000], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: motif
      bars: 11
      grid: dilla
      voices: [kick, snare, ghost, hat, open_hat]
      density: 1.0
      drums: [humanize, swing]
      hate: { profile: hardgroove, elements: [hat, clap, perc_a, perc_b] }
      lead: []
      gains_db: { texture: -10, kit: 0, hate: -10, bass: 0, pads: -2, lead: 0 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [16000, 16000], hate: [10000, 10000], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: mutation
      bars: 11
      grid: flylo
      voices: [kick, snare, ghost, hat, open_hat]
      density: 1.0
      drums: [swing, ghost, ratchet, accent, stutter]
      hate: { profile: hardgroove, elements: [hat, open, clap, perc_a, perc_b] }
      lead: [ratchet, stutter]
      kick_drop: [10]
      gains_db: { texture: -10, kit: 0, hate: -6, bass: 0, pads: -4, lead: -1 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [2500, 16000], hate: [1500, 16000], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: hate
      bars: 16
      grid: techno
      voices: [snare, ghost, hat, open_hat]
      density: 0.9
      drums: [humanize, ghost, drop]
      hate: { profile: industrial, elements: [kick, hat, clap, perc_a, perc_b, texture] }
      lead: [chop, repeat]
      gains_db: { texture: -12, kit: -5, hate: 0, bass: -2, pads: -10, lead: -8 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [16000, 16000], hate: [16000, 16000], pads: [1500, 1500] }
    - name: breakdown
      bars: 11
      grid: dilla
      voices: [kick, ghost, hat]
      density: 0.45
      drums: [humanize, drop]
      hate: { profile: basic_channel, elements: [perc_b, texture] }
      lead: []
      kick_drop: [0]
      gains_db: { texture: -5, kit: -3, hate: -14, bass: -60, pads: -1, lead: -60 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [1400, 1400], hate: [2000, 2000], pads: [1200, 6000] }
    - name: mirrored
      bars: 11
      grid: flylo
      voices: [kick, ghost, hat]
      density: 0.6
      drums: [shift, humanize, probabilize]
      hate: { profile: detroit, elements: [hat, perc_a, perc_b] }
      harmony: mirrored
      lead: []
      kick_drop: [10]
      gains_db: { texture: -6, kit: -1, hate: -10, bass: 0, pads: 0, lead: -60 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [3000, 8000], hate: [4000, 8000], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: return
      bars: 16
      grid: dilla
      voices: [kick, snare, ghost, hat, open_hat]
      density: 1.0
      drums: [swing, accent, ghost]
      hate: { profile: industrial, elements: [kick, hat, clap, perc_a, perc_b] }
      lead: [reverse, invert]
      gains_db: { texture: -10, kit: 0, hate: -4, bass: 0, pads: -3, lead: 0 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [16000, 16000], hate: [16000, 16000], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: everything
      bars: 11
      grid: techno
      voices: [kick, snare, ghost, hat, open_hat]
      density: 1.0
      drums: [swing, ghost, ratchet, accent, quantize]
      hate: { profile: industrial, elements: [kick, hat, open, clap, perc_a, perc_b, texture] }
      lead: [transpose]
      gains_db: { texture: -8, kit: 0, hate: -3, bass: 0, pads: -2, lead: 0 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [16000, 16000], hate: [16000, 16000], pads: [16000, 16000] }
    - name: decay
      bars: 8
      grid: dilla
      voices: [kick, hat]
      density: 0.4
      drums: [humanize, probabilize]
      hate: { profile: basic_channel, elements: [perc_b, texture] }
      lead: [stretch, resample]
      gains_db: { texture: -3, kit: -3, hate: -12, bass: -60, pads: -6, lead: -8 }
      cutoff_hz: { kit: [6000, 400], hate: [4000, 500], pads: [4000, 700] }

`````

### dilla/data/dilla_reference.yml

`````yaml
# dilla_reference.yml — sourced material and quality gates for the Dilla
# engine, pulled from documented interviews, track analysis, and producer
# consensus (Dan Charnas "Dilla Time"; Ethan Hein analyses; forum/tutorial
# consensus on MPC-era mixing). Read by lib/, not by dilla.rb — two loaders,
# each taking one section:
#   - documented_progressions merge into HARMONY_PROFILES, loaded by
#     lib/groove.rb (see the load near CHORD_VOICINGS) as additive
#     entries — existing named profiles (e.g. slum_players,
#     chromatic_mediant_drift) are NOT overwritten, since some are original
#     Dilla/FlyLo-inspired compositions rather than direct transcriptions.
#   - loss_gates are hard reject thresholds checked before a take is promoted
#     into project/promoted_profiles.json, loaded by lib/listen.rb
#     as REFERENCE_PATH and applied via DillaMaster.passes_loss_gates?, which
#     dilla.rb calls at the stream and promotion sites.
#   - principles is the research the two above were written from: what
#     the groove, harmony, sampling and mix are for, with the evidence level
#     of each claim. No code reads it; it is the argument a change to the
#     sound answers to.
#
# Chord symbols are limited to what DillaLofiMachine.chord_from_symbol can
# parse (see CHORD_SUFFIXES / CHORD_VOICINGS in lib/groove.rb) — a few
# symbols here were simplified from the original documented voicing (13th ->
# 7th, alt tensions spelled as "alt") either because that exact extension
# isn't in the parser's vocabulary, or because DillaMusicGems (the major_third_cycle_full
# gem adapter) hangs on the literal symbol. See the "source_note" per entry.

documented_progressions:
  slum_village_players_documented:
    producer: dilla
    key: "C minor"
    bpm: 91
    swing: 56
    chord_bars: 2
    phrase_bars: 16
    voicing: rootless
    chords: [Cm9, Fm9, Bb13, Ebmaj7, Abmaj7, Dm7b5, G7alt, Cm9]
    source: "Slum Village - Fantastic Vol. 2, 'Players' (documented track analysis)"
    source_note: "Bb13 restored — the parser gained 13 since this was simplified to Bb7, and the 13th is the soul colour the simplification removed. G7#5#9 stays spelled G7alt, which already covers both tensions."

  slum_village_intro_documented:
    producer: dilla
    key: "C minor"
    bpm: 91
    swing: 56
    chord_bars: 2
    phrase_bars: 8
    voicing: rootless
    chords: [Cm9, Fm9, Bb13, Ebmaj7]
    source: "Slum Village - Fantastic Vol. 2, 'Intro'"
    source_note: "Bb13 restored, same as Players above."

  flylo_beginners_falafel_documented:
    producer: flylo
    key: "C major"
    bpm: 86
    swing: 54
    chord_bars: 2
    phrase_bars: 8
    voicing: rootless
    chords: [Dm9, G13, Cmaj9, Fmaj7]
    source: "Flying Lotus - Los Angeles, 'Beginners Falafel'"
    source_note: "G13 restored — parseable now."

  flylo_camel_documented:
    producer: flylo
    key: "C major"
    bpm: 86
    swing: 54
    chord_bars: 2
    phrase_bars: 8
    voicing: rootless
    chords: [Dm9, G13, Cmaj9, Fmaj7#11]
    source: "Flying Lotus - Los Angeles, 'Camel'"
    source_note: "Fmaj7#11 and G13 restored — both parse now. The #11 is the lydian shimmer that distinguishes this from Beginners Falafel; with both simplified the two entries were byte-identical in harmony. Still distinct from the chromatic_mediant_drift/quartal_west_coast profiles used by RENDER_MODE=camel, which are original compositions rather than transcriptions."

# Hard pre-flight rejects, not just advisory scores — a take failing any of
# these should not be promoted even if beauty/groove scored well.
loss_gates:
  crest_factor_min_db: 6.0
  source: "peak-to-RMS below 6dB reads as over-compressed/lacking punch"
  mud_max_db_200_400hz: -12.0
  mud_source: "sustained energy above -12dBFS in the 200-400Hz 'mud zone' masks snare body"
  kick_bass_correlation_max: 0.95
  correlation_source: "kick/bass micro-timing correlation above 0.95 reads as quantized/robotic"
  stereo_phase_correlation_min: 0.30
  phase_source: "L/R phase correlation below 0.30 anywhere risks cancellation when summed to mono (phone/laptop speakers, club mono sends)"
  # Same window dilla_quality already warns on: ±1.5 dB around MASTER_LUFS_BY_STYLE
  # (currently -19..-14). Written here so promotion and `quality` share one
  # source; test_loss_gates_share_the_quality_lufs_window fails if they drift.
  true_peak_max_dbtp: -1.0
  true_peak_source: "EBU R128 / streaming delivery; above -1 dBTP intersamples clip on lossy codecs"
  integrated_lufs_min: -20.5
  integrated_lufs_max: -12.5
  lufs_source: "DILLA_QUALITY_LUFS_TARGET: style spread -19..-14 plus 1.5 dB tolerance"

principles:
  version: 0.1.0
  status: draft
  purpose: >
    Research-backed knowledge specification describing the aesthetic,
    workflow, and musical principles associated with J Dilla. This file
    distinguishes documented evidence from inference and is intended to
    guide AI systems toward creating original music inspired by these
    principles rather than imitation.

  metadata:
    evidence_levels:
      documented: "Supported by interviews, Dilla Time, collaborators, or primary sources."
      consensus: "Broad producer consensus."
      analysis: "Derived from careful musical analysis."
      hypothesis: "Reasonable inference requiring validation."

  identity:
    artist: J Dilla
    legal_name: James Dewitt Yancey
    birthplace: Detroit, Michigan
    core_values:
      - groove_over_precision
      - emotion_over_complexity
      - transformation_over_reproduction
      - restraint_over_density

  philosophy:
    principles:
      - Every instrument owns its own sense of time.
      - Groove emerges from relationships between events.
      - Silence is musical material.
      - Sampling transforms memory into something new.
      - Remove notes before adding notes.
      - Preserve humanity over perfection.

  historical_context:
    influences:
      detroit:
        - Motown
        - James Jamerson
        - Amp Fiddler
        - Slum Village
      jazz:
        - Ahmad Jamal
        - Herbie Hancock
        - Roy Ayers
        - Donald Byrd
        - Weldon Irvine
      funk:
        - Bernard Purdie
        - Clyde Stubblefield
        - Zigaboo Modeliste

  groove_engine:
    objective: >
      Produce independent rhythmic layers that repeatedly converge and diverge
      while remaining danceable.
    rules:
      - Avoid identical timing offsets on every hit.
      - Favor phrase-level drift over random jitter.
      - Model kick, snare, hats, bass, and samples as independent clocks.
      - Preserve intentional asymmetry.
      - Do not rely on a fixed swing percentage.

  sampling_engine:
    philosophy:
      - Choose emotionally compelling material.
      - Transform more than copy.
      - Preserve texture when possible.
    operations:
      - chop
      - resample
      - pitch
      - filter
      - reverse_tail
      - truncate
      - layer

  harmony:
    goals:
      - ambiguity
      - color
      - warmth
      - incomplete_resolution
    preferences:
      - extended_chords
      - rootless_voicings
      - suspended_motion
      - modal_borrowing

  drums:
    priorities:
      - head_nod
      - conversational_kick_snare
      - dynamic_velocity
      - ghost_notes

  bass:
    relationship:
      follows:
        - groove
        - harmony
      not:
        - rigid_grid

  arrangement:
    patterns:
      - introduce_small_changes
      - remove_elements
      - filter_transitions
      - surprise_without_breaking_flow

  mixing:
    goals:
      - warmth
      - depth
      - punch
      - clarity
    avoid:
      - over_limiting
      - excessive_brightness
      - sterile_perfection

  critic:
    scorecard:
      groove: 0.0
      humanity: 0.0
      emotional_depth: 0.0
      originality: 0.0
      restraint: 0.0
    acceptance:
      groove: ">=0.95"
      humanity: ">=0.90"
      emotional_depth: ">=0.90"

  anti_patterns:
    - quantize_everything
    - maximize_loudness
    - overcompress
    - copy_reference_track
    - endless_layering
    - predictable_arrangement

  generation_pipeline:
    - collect_influences
    - establish_groove
    - add_harmony
    - transform_samples
    - simplify
    - critique
    - humanize
    - simplify_again
    - final_review

  bibliography:
    primary:
      - "Dan Charnas: Dilla Time"
      - "Interviews with Questlove"
      - "Interviews with Karriem Riggins"
      - "Interviews with Amp Fiddler"
    note: >
      This specification intentionally separates documented facts from
      analytical inference and should evolve as new research appears.

`````

### dilla/data/live.yml

`````yaml
# reader: LiveSynth (lib/livesets.rb)
#
# The live synthesiser: AnalogSynth's patches and the Model D panels in
# model_d.yml, played straight to the sound card as they are generated.
#
#   ruby dilla.rb live default              MASTER's main sound, until `live stop`
#   ruby dilla.rb live improvise            the improviser with drums, dub and FM
#   ruby dilla.rb live progression [name]   a named progression, looped
#   ruby dilla.rb live patch <name>         one patch's own phrase
#   ruby dilla.rb live say "<sentence>"     what MASTER sends
#
# MASTER's generic "play" is the steerable moog_improv showcase:
# walking harmony, rotating pads and basses, DFAM, arp and its full analogue
# rack. Explicit `live default` still runs liveset.rb, the take the operator
# froze on 2026-09-24, unchanged.
# The approved takes remain in takes/: soul_jazz_six is
# takes/loved_moog_loop.rb, moog_dfam takes/moog_dfam_loop.rb, and
# moog_improv takes/liveset_db4ddf1a.rb, each before any ffmpeg console.
# Those frozen numbers change only on the operator's word.
stream:
  rate: 32000
  block_frames: 1024
  # Every sample leaves through tanh(s * drive), scaled under full scale.
  master_drive: 1.4
  master_scale: 26000
  # Each note sits this many cents off concert pitch, drawn per note, so a
  # chord beats like a played instrument rather than a printed one.
  note_drift_cents: 0.7
  cutoff_clamp: [30, 12000]
  # A left-channel share per role; the rest goes right.
  pan: { pad: 0.52, bass: 0.52, lead: 0.42 }
  # How long the last notes ring after the music ends on its own.
  tail_seconds: 2.5
  # Asked to stop, it fades out over this instead of ringing on.
  stop_fade_seconds: 0.4

# Knob changes asked for by name, and how long "slowly" is.
automation:
  speeds: { slowly: 30, gradually: 20, gently: 15, quickly: 3, suddenly: 0.5 }
  default_seconds: 10
  # One word of "open the filter" moves a knob this far on its 0-1 travel.
  step: 0.35
  # A patch change arrives over this many chords instead of on one, so the
  # knobs of the old patch turn into the new one's.
  crossfade_chords: 2

progressions:
  # The first progression the operator heard live: soul-jazz in F minor, the
  # bass on the root and each voicing written out, played on a pad that
  # changes every two chords.
  soul_jazz_six:
    bar_seconds: 4.4
    pad_every: 2
    pads: [warm_pad, poly_strings, prophet_five, juno_pad]
    bass_patch: moog_bass
    pad_gain: 0.22
    # [offset in the bar, held, gain]: the root, then again a little late.
    bass_hits: [[0.0, 1.6, 0.55], [2.35, 1.2, 0.45]]
    chords:
      - { name: Fm9, bass: 41, tones: [56, 60, 63, 67] }
      - { name: Bbm9, bass: 46, tones: [56, 61, 65, 68] }
      - { name: Eb13, bass: 39, tones: [55, 60, 61, 65] }
      - { name: Abmaj9, bass: 44, tones: [55, 60, 63, 70] }
      - { name: Dbmaj7#11, bass: 37, tones: [60, 65, 67, 72] }
      - { name: C7alt, bass: 36, tones: [58, 61, 64, 68] }
    knobs:
      cutoff: { sine_seconds: 23, phase: 0.0, centre: 0.55, depth: 0.45 }
      resonance: { sine_seconds: 31, phase: 1.3, centre: 0.5, depth: 0.5 }
    # How a knob at 0-1 bends each role's patch: cutoff is scaled by
    # base + knob * span; resonance gains knob * span, held under ceiling.
    response:
      pad: { cutoff: [0.35, 1.6], resonance: [0.45, 0.85] }
      bass: { cutoff: [0.7, 0.8], resonance: [0.0, null] }
  # The first sound the operator froze on 2026-09-24 ("FREEZE THAT SOUND"):
  # soul_jazz_six with a DFAM under it, twice round, as takes/moog_dfam_loop.rb
  # plays it. test_dilla_live_synth pins these numbers to that file.
  moog_dfam:
    from: soul_jazz_six
    loops: 2
    # The DFAM as the Moog is built: an 8-step sequencer running in
    # sixteenths of the bar, each step its own pitch and velocity, starting
    # from DfamEngine::DEFAULT_PATTERN, one step mutating every mutate_every
    # steps. VCO 1, a triangle, frequency-modulates VCO 2, a square; both
    # fall from pitch_env.depth + 1 times their pitch over pitch_env.seconds;
    # noise is mixed in; a ladder low-pass with its own decay, then the VCA's.
    # Decays and cutoff drift on slow sines, like the pads' knobs.
    dfam:
      level: 0.34
      steps_per_bar: 16
      mutate_every: 32
      mutate: { pitch_reach: 18, pitch_range: [5, 95], mute_odds: 0.15, velocity_reach: 20, velocity_range: [35, 100] }
      base_hz: 40.0
      octaves: 3.0
      pan: [0.35, 0.3]
      pitch_env: { depth: 2.2, seconds: 0.045 }
      vco2_ratio: 1.5
      fm: 0.45
      mix: { triangle: 0.55, square: 0.3, noise: 0.18 }
      cutoff_floor: 120.0
      resonance: 0.55
      # floor + span * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(2 pi t / sine_seconds + phase))
      knobs:
        vcf_decay: { floor: 0.05, span: 0.1, sine_seconds: 37.0, phase: 0.0 }
        vca_decay: { floor: 0.09, span: 0.12, sine_seconds: 29.0, phase: 0.7 }
        cutoff: { floor: 900.0, span: 2600.0, sine_seconds: 43.0, phase: 2.1 }
      # A hit leaves once this many VCA decays have passed.
      life_decays: 8
  # The standard default before liveset.rb, as takes/liveset_db4ddf1a.rb
  # plays it (the operator froze it on 2026-09-24). moog_dfam improvising:
  # the loved six chords open it, then the chords are walked
  # (improvise.moves) with four-tone rootless voicings nearest the last, and
  # it goes round until stopped. The pad changes every chord, the bass every
  # bass_every chords, an arpeggio rides some chords, the DFAM runs at 1.5x
  # the groove with accents, a five-step sequence against its eight, and a
  # kick, and the whole stream leaves through the console named in `master`.
  moog_improv:
    from: moog_dfam
    loops: 0
    walk:
      key: 5
      start: [0, m9]
      voicing_range: [53, 74]
      modulate_every: 24
      modulate_by: [5, 3, 8, 10]
    pads: [warm_pad, poly_strings, prophet_five, juno_pad, prophet_pad, vp330_ensemble, soft_reed, e_piano, rhodes_tine, glass_bell]
    pad_every: 1
    basses: [moog_bass, acid, sub, dub_bass]
    bass_every: 4
    # Sixteenths an octave above the voicing, up, down, up-down or shuffled.
    arp: { odds: 0.3, patches: [glass_bell, e_piano, poly_lead, vapor_lead], steps: 16, octave: 12, held: 0.7, gain: 0.1 }
    # moog_dfam's DFAM, in 24ths of the bar where it ran in 16ths -- the
    # groove at one and a half times, the chords where they were -- with
    # these added.
    dfam:
      steps_per_bar: 24
      # The downbeat and the and-of-two lean in.
      accent: [1.35, 0.8, 1.0, 0.85, 1.25, 0.8, 1.1, 0.9]
      # Five steps against eight, a hair behind, quieter, panned wide.
      second: { pitch: [78, 64, 88, 70, 92], velocity: [55, 0, 70, 45, 60], late_seconds: 0.004, gain: 0.55, pan: [0.25, 0.75] }
      # A sub on every beat -- four steps of the sequencer -- falling from
      # base_hz + drop_hz to base_hz, into tanh.
      kick: { every: 4, level: 0.34, drive: 2.8, base_hz: 45.0, drop_hz: 105.0, drop_seconds: 0.035, decay_seconds: 0.32, click: 0.5, click_seconds: 0.005, length_seconds: 0.5 }
    # The showcase rack: four consecutive Nasty VCS phases, three heavy
    # Sonitex STX-1260 passes and a measured three-stage console summing stack.
    # VCS stays level-neutral; the 1260 passes progressively harder reduction and
    # sample-rate damage. The final limiter is only gain protection.
    master:
      - { vcs: { depth: 0.34, smear: 2.4, db: 0.0 } }
      - { sonitex: { bits: 12, lo: 40, hi: 13000, drive: 1.12, mix: 0.72 } }
      - { vcs: { depth: 0.28, smear: 2.8, db: 0.0 } }
      - { sonitex: { bits: 11, lo: 42, hi: 12000, drive: 1.16, mix: 0.82, samples: 2 } }
      - { vcs: { depth: 0.4, smear: 1.9, db: 0.0 } }
      - { console_stack: { instances: 3, offset: 0.10, param: 1.2, speed: 0.1 } }
      - { sonitex: { bits: 10, lo: 48, hi: 11000, drive: 1.22, mix: 0.95, samples: 2 } }
      - { vcs: { depth: 0.3, smear: 3.6, db: 0.0 } }
      - { program_memory: { threshold: -18, ratio: 1.2, attack: 12, release: 420 } }
      - { filter: "alimiter=limit=0.95" }
  # MASTER's Theory calls i7 iv7 bVII7 bVI7 dilla_love; these are its chords
  # in C with the ninths and the thirteenth dilla voices them with. A
  # progression that names its chords instead of writing voicings is voiced
  # nearest-note, and takes everything else from soul_jazz_six.
  dilla_love:
    names: [Cm9, Fm9, Bb13, Abmaj9]

  # Verified Melody A.M.-era chord cells from royksopp.rb, rendered through the
  # same steerable DFAM/progression/session path as every other live set.
  royksopp_live:
    from: moog_dfam
    loops: 0
    bar_seconds: 4.486
    pad_every: 2
    pads: [juno_pad, vp330_ensemble, e_piano, rhodes_tine, prophet_pad]
    bass_patch: moog_bass
    pad_gain: 0.24
    bass_hits: [[0.0, 2.2, 0.52], [2.35, 1.1, 0.38]]
    master:
      - { vcs: { depth: 0.34, smear: 2.4, db: 0.0 } }
      - { sonitex: { bits: 12, lo: 40, hi: 13000, drive: 1.12, mix: 0.72 } }
      - { vcs: { depth: 0.28, smear: 2.8, db: 0.0 } }
      - { sonitex: { bits: 11, lo: 42, hi: 12000, drive: 1.16, mix: 0.82, samples: 2 } }
      - { vcs: { depth: 0.4, smear: 1.9, db: 0.0 } }
      - { console_stack: { instances: 3, offset: 0.10, param: 1.2, speed: 0.1 } }
      - { sonitex: { bits: 10, lo: 48, hi: 11000, drive: 1.22, mix: 0.95, samples: 2 } }
      - { vcs: { depth: 0.3, smear: 3.6, db: 0.0 } }
      - { filter: "alimiter=limit=0.95" }
# Any name in CHORD_PROGRESSIONS plays too, voiced the same way.

# What `live patch <name>` plays for a patch that carries no phrase of its
# own, by the part the patch plays.
demos:
  bass: { step: 0.26, gate: 0.75, gain: 0.55, notes: [C2, C2, C3, D#2, F2, F2, G2, A#1, C2, C2, C3, D#2, G2, F2, D#2, A#1] }
  lead: { step: 0.34, gate: 0.9, gain: 0.3, notes: [C5, D#5, G5, A#5, G5, F5, D#5, F5, G5, C6, A#5, G5] }
  pad: { step: 4.4, gate: 0.95, gain: 0.22, notes: [[G#3, C4, D#4, G4], [G#3, C#4, F4, G#4], [G3, C4, C#4, F4], [G3, C4, D#4, A#4]] }

improvise:
  bpm: 96
  bpm_spread: 3
  # The kit, written a chord at a time with the chord. "drums off" stops it.
  drums: true
  # The kick on every beat, doubled with ghost hits between beats, and now
  # and then a roll into the next chord that tightens from sixteenths to
  # 32nds. Each hit is a sine falling from base_hz + drop_hz to base_hz over
  # drop_seconds, dying over decay_seconds, with a click on top, in closed
  # form so every hit is the same hit. The hits sum on a bus driven hard into
  # tanh, and the kick rides its own channels past every effect.
  kick:
    level: 0.55
    base_hz: 48.0
    drop_hz: 110.0
    drop_seconds: 0.04
    decay_seconds: 0.26
    click: 0.3
    click_seconds: 0.004
    length_seconds: 0.6
    bus_drive: 3.2
    bus_gain: 0.62
    # [odds, fraction of a beat after it, gain]
    ghosts: [[0.55, 0.5, 0.62], [0.35, 0.75, 0.5], [0.2, 0.25, 0.4]]
    roll_odds: 0.45
    roll_gains: [[0.45, 0.08], [0.6, 0.08]]
  # A clap on two and four, a hair late as a hand plays it, with ghosts:
  # three band-passed noise bursts 11 ms apart, a tail, and a 185 Hz body.
  snare:
    level: 0.5
    late_seconds: 0.012
    # A ghost on the "and-a" of any beat, and one on the "e" of one and three.
    ghosts:
      - { odds: 0.3, at: 0.75, gain: 0.28 }
      - { odds: 0.2, at: 0.25, gain: 0.22, even_beats: true }
    burst_gap_seconds: 0.011
    burst_seconds: 0.006
    tail_seconds: 0.13
    tail_gain: 0.6
    body_hz: 185.0
    body_seconds: 0.05
    length_seconds: 0.4
    # The band-pass: a state-variable filter at about 1.4 kHz.
    filter_f: 0.26
    filter_damping: 0.55
    drive: 1.5
    pan: 0.48
  # The whole stream goes out through ffmpeg: the music twice, once through
  # dilla's warm_dilla_pad_post synth chain (warm_dilla_pad_synth_filters at
  # these values) and once through a dub send -- highpass, three tape heads at
  # the beat fractions, an eighth echo, chorus, lowpass -- mixed with the dry
  # kick. <N> in the send is N ms per beat. "more dub" turns the dub knob.
  post:
    chain: { lowpass: 3400, mud_db: 0.0, upper_mud_db: 0.0, tremolo: true }
    dub: "highpass=f=180,lowpass=f=2600,aecho=0.85:0.9:<750>|<1000>|<1500>:0.55|0.45|0.35,aecho=0.8:0.85:<375>:0.5,chorus=0.8:0.9:45:0.4:0.3:1.5,lowpass=f=2200,volume=0.9"
    limit: 0.96
  # Keys the walk starts in, as semitones above C; every one is minor.
  keys: [5, 0, 3, 10, 8]
  start: [0, m9]
  # The walk: from [degree, quality], where it tends to go next. Degrees are
  # semitones above the key; qualities are DillaImprovisation::QUALITIES.
  moves:
    - { from: [0, m9], to: [[5, m9], [10, "13"], [8, maj9], [5, m11], [3, maj9]] }
    - { from: [0, m11], to: [[5, m9], [8, "maj7#11"], [10, 13sus]] }
    - { from: [5, m9], to: [[10, "13"], [7, 7alt], [3, maj9], [0, m6/9]] }
    - { from: [5, m11], to: [[10, "13"], [7, 7alt]] }
    - { from: [10, "13"], to: [[3, maj9], [8, maj9], [0, m9]] }
    - { from: [10, 13sus], to: [[10, "13"], [3, maj9]] }
    - { from: [3, maj9], to: [[8, maj9], [5, m9], [1, "maj7#11"]] }
    - { from: [8, maj9], to: [[1, "maj7#11"], [7, 7alt], [5, m9]] }
    - { from: [8, "maj7#11"], to: [[7, 7alt], [1, "maj7#11"]] }
    - { from: [1, "maj7#11"], to: [[7, 7alt], [0, m9], [0, m11]] }
    - { from: [7, 7alt], to: [[0, m9], [0, m11], [8, maj9]] }
    - { from: [0, m6/9], to: [[5, m9], [10, "13"]] }
  # Voicings stay between F3 and D5, each voice moving to the nearest tone.
  voicing_range: [48, 76]
  first_voicing: [55, 60, 63, 67, 70]
  # The next chord is written this far ahead of the playhead.
  lookahead_seconds: 1.0
  first_chord_at: 0.3
  two_bar_odds: 0.35
  pads: [warm_pad, poly_strings, prophet_five, juno_pad, prophet_pad, vp330_ensemble, rhodes_tine, surreal_wash]
  # Leads are off until asked for ("lead on", "fm lead"); on, they come and go
  # by themselves. A lead is an FM preset below or any patch by name.
  lead_enabled: false
  leads: [bell, metal, growl, glass, chaos, drone]
  # Two-operator FM (AnalogSynth::FmVoice): the modulator's ratio to the note,
  # the index and how fast it falls, the modulator's feedback, and the
  # envelope. The order is the order a lead is drawn from.
  fm:
    bell: { ratio: 3.5, index: 6.0, index_decay: 0.7, fb: 0.0, attack: 0.002, decay: 1.6 }
    metal: { ratio: 1.414, index: 4.5, index_decay: 1.2, fb: 0.55, attack: 0.004, decay: 0.9 }
    growl: { ratio: 0.5, index: 3.2, index_decay: 3.0, fb: 0.3, attack: 0.08, decay: 1.4 }
    glass: { ratio: 7.02, index: 2.4, index_decay: 0.25, fb: 0.0, attack: 0.001, decay: 0.7 }
    chaos: { ratio: 2.76, index: 8.0, index_decay: 0.4, fb: 0.9, attack: 0.003, decay: 0.5 }
    drone: { ratio: 1.001, index: 1.8, index_decay: 6.0, fb: 0.2, attack: 0.6, decay: 3.0 }
  fm_phrase: { odds: 0.6, gain: 0.12, range: [48, 90], reach: 9, steps: [0.25, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0], held: 0.8 }
  bass_patch: moog_bass
  # "Play it on moog patches": the same walk with one family's instruments.
  # moog is the Model D panels in model_d.yml; prophet and rhodes are the
  # AnalogSynth patches bed.yml plays those families on.
  families:
    moog: { pads: [moog_strings, moog_brass, lofi_pad], leads: [minimoog_lead, lucky_man, moog_flute, moog_pluck], bass_patch: fat_bass }
    prophet: { pads: [prophet_five, prophet_pad, juno_pad, vp330_ensemble], leads: [poly_lead, vapor_lead], bass_patch: moog_bass }
    rhodes: { pads: [rhodes_tine, e_piano], leads: [glass_bell, soft_reed], bass_patch: dub_bass }
  pad_gain: 0.2
  pad_chords: [3, 6]
  lead_toggle_odds: 0.18
  lead_gain: 0.14
  lead_odds: 0.72
  lead_range: [64, 88]
  lead_swing_seconds: 0.06
  modulate_every: 16
  modulate_by: [5, 3, 8, 10]
  # Dilla: the bass sits behind the beat.
  bass_late_seconds: 0.035
  knobs:
    cutoff: { start: 0.5, speed: 0.05 }
    resonance: { start: 0.4, speed: 0.04 }
    detune: { start: 0.5, speed: 0.03 }
    # How much of the music reaches the dub send; it holds still until asked.
    dub: { start: 0.7 }
  # A walk keeps its velocity by this much a block and is pulled toward the
  # middle by this much, so it wanders for tens of seconds and comes back.
  walk_damping: 0.995
  walk_pull: 0.02
  response:
    pad: { cutoff: [0.35, 1.7], resonance: [0.5, 0.88], detune: 0.004 }
    bass: { cutoff: [0.7, 0.9], resonance: [0.15, null], detune: 0.004 }
    lead: { cutoff: [0.8, 0.8], resonance: [0.15, null], detune: 0.004 }

`````

### dilla/data/model_d.yml

`````yaml
# reader: AnalogSynth::ModelD (lib/sound.rb)
#
# Minimoog Model D patches, written as the front panel is set: footages,
# waveforms, 0-10 dials, the cutoff's -5..+5 scale, switches. That is how the
# sound charts write a patch and how a player reads one. AnalogSynth::ModelD
# turns the dials into hertz, seconds and gains, in one place, and plays them
# through the same ladder as every other patch in the engine.
#
# The settings follow the classic sound-chart patches from memory of the
# published charts, not a transcription of them; a player with the book can
# correct a dial here and nothing else changes.
#
#   oscillators   osc1, osc2: triangle tri_saw saw square wide_pulse narrow_pulse
#                 osc3: triangle reverse_saw saw square wide_pulse narrow_pulse
#                 range LO 32' 16' 8' 4' 2'; frequency is OSC 2 and 3's tune dial
#                 in semitones (-7..+7); keyboard_control: false frees OSC 3 from
#                 the keys, which with LO makes it the modulation oscillator
#   mixer         0-10 per source; external is the output patched back into the
#                 mixer, the Model D's overdrive trick
#   filter        cutoff -5..+5, emphasis 0-10 (10 sings on its own),
#                 contour_amount 0-10, keyboard_control_1/2 switches, and the
#                 filter contour's attack, decay, sustain
#   loudness      the loudness contour's attack, decay, sustain
#   controllers   glide 0-10, mod_mix 0 (OSC 3) to 10 (noise), osc_mod and
#                 filter_mod switches, wheel 0-10, decay_switch
#   demo          what `live patch <name>` plays: a note or a chord per step
patches:
  fat_bass:
    aliases: [fat bass, moog bass, minimoog bass, bass]
    oscillators:
      osc1: { range: "32'", wave: saw }
      osc2: { range: "16'", wave: saw, frequency: 0.05 }
      osc3: { range: "16'", wave: square, frequency: -0.08 }
    mixer: { osc1: 10, osc2: 8, osc3: 7, noise: 0, external: 0 }
    filter: { cutoff: -3.0, emphasis: 2, contour_amount: 7, keyboard_control_1: true, keyboard_control_2: false, attack: 0, decay: 3, sustain: 3 }
    loudness: { attack: 0, decay: 5, sustain: 8 }
    controllers: { glide: 0, mod_mix: 0, osc_mod: false, filter_mod: false, wheel: 0, decay_switch: false }
    volume: 8
    demo: { step: 0.26, gate: 0.75, notes: [C2, C2, C3, D#2, F2, F2, G2, A#1, C2, C2, C3, D#2, G2, F2, D#2, A#1] }
  funk_bass:
    aliases: [funk bass, funky bass, worrell]
    oscillators:
      osc1: { range: "16'", wave: square }
      osc2: { range: "16'", wave: saw, frequency: 0.05 }
      osc3: { range: "32'", wave: narrow_pulse }
    mixer: { osc1: 9, osc2: 7, osc3: 0, noise: 0, external: 4 }
    filter: { cutoff: -2.0, emphasis: 6, contour_amount: 6, keyboard_control_1: true, keyboard_control_2: false, attack: 0, decay: 2.5, sustain: 0 }
    loudness: { attack: 0, decay: 3.5, sustain: 6 }
    controllers: { glide: 2, mod_mix: 0, osc_mod: false, filter_mod: false, wheel: 0, decay_switch: false }
    volume: 8
    demo: { step: 0.2, gate: 0.6, notes: [E1, E2, E1, G1, A1, A#1, B1, E2, D2, E1, E1, G1, A1, D2, B1, A1] }
  minimoog_lead:
    aliases: [minimoog lead, moog lead, lead, solo]
    legato: true
    oscillators:
      osc1: { range: "16'", wave: saw }
      osc2: { range: "8'", wave: saw, frequency: 0.07 }
      osc3: { range: LO, wave: triangle, frequency: 3, keyboard_control: false }
    mixer: { osc1: 9, osc2: 7, osc3: 0, noise: 0, external: 0 }
    filter: { cutoff: 0, emphasis: 4, contour_amount: 5, keyboard_control_1: true, keyboard_control_2: true, attack: 1, decay: 5, sustain: 5 }
    loudness: { attack: 0.5, decay: 5, sustain: 9 }
    controllers: { glide: 5, mod_mix: 0, osc_mod: true, filter_mod: false, wheel: 1.5, decay_switch: true }
    volume: 7
    demo: { step: 0.34, gate: 1.0, notes: [C4, D#4, G4, A#4, G4, F4, D#4, F4, G4, C5, A#4, G4, F4, D#4, C4] }
  lucky_man:
    aliases: [lucky man, emerson, portamento lead, glide lead]
    legato: true
    oscillators:
      osc1: { range: "8'", wave: saw }
      osc2: { range: "8'", wave: square, frequency: 0.1 }
      osc3: { range: LO, wave: triangle, frequency: 3, keyboard_control: false }
    mixer: { osc1: 8, osc2: 8, osc3: 0, noise: 0, external: 0 }
    filter: { cutoff: 1.0, emphasis: 3, contour_amount: 3, keyboard_control_1: true, keyboard_control_2: true, attack: 2, decay: 6, sustain: 7 }
    loudness: { attack: 1, decay: 6, sustain: 10 }

  lofi_pad:

    voices: 5

    mixer: { osc1: 8, osc2: 8, osc3: 0, noise: 1, noise_color: pink, external: 1.5 }
    filter: { cutoff: -1.0, emphasis: 1.8, contour_amount: 2, keyboard_control_1: true, keyboard_control_2: false, attack: 7, decay: 7, sustain: 6 }
    loudness: { attack: 7, decay: 7, sustain: 8.5 }
`````

### dilla/data/modes.yml

`````yaml
# The modes the harmony spine can walk, and what walking each one means.
#
# dilla.rb builds SCALE_SEMITONES, SCALE_DEGREE_QUALITY and MODE_TRANSITIONS
# from this file at load, and refuses to load if a mode names a degree its scale
# does not have. `mode:` in the progression walks comes from GEN_MODE, minor by
# default, so a generated style set to GEN_MODE=tizita walks that qenit. Every
# walk indexes a scale by its own length, which is what lets a five-note mode
# sit beside the two seven-note ones.
#
# A mode here declares three things and they are checked against each other:
#
#   semitones   the scale, from the root, ascending, no octave. Its LENGTH is
#               the degree count; nothing assumes seven.
#   qualities   degree -> chord quality. One entry per degree, no gaps.
#   transitions degree -> {next_degree => relative weight}. The functional
#               motion. Every degree named must exist in the scale.
#
# Sources are recorded per mode because two of them disagree, and a table that
# hides a disagreement is how the engine ended up with two CHORD_TEMPLATES that
# said different things about 7alt.

modes:
  # The two functional modes, held to the same shape as the pentatonic ones so
  # that adding a mode is one edit. test_dilla_chord_theory.rb pins their values.
  major:
    semitones: [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11]
    qualities: { 1: maj9, 2: m9, 3: m7, 4: maj9, 5: "7", 6: m9, 7: dim }
    # Tonic radiates outward, predominants (ii/IV) gravitate to the dominant,
    # the dominant resolves home, vi is the deceptive detour.
    transitions:
      1: { 4: 3, 5: 3, 6: 2, 2: 1 }
      2: { 5: 4, 7: 1, 4: 1 }
      3: { 6: 2, 4: 1, 2: 1 }
      4: { 5: 3, 1: 2, 2: 1 }
      5: { 1: 4, 6: 1, 4: 1 }
      6: { 2: 2, 4: 2, 5: 1 }
      7: { 1: 3, 3: 1 }
    source: functional harmony

  minor:
    semitones: [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]
    qualities: { 1: m9, 2: dim, 3: maj9, 4: m9, 5: "7", 6: maj9, 7: "7" }
    transitions:
      1: { 4: 3, 5: 3, 6: 2, 2: 1 }
      2: { 5: 4, 7: 1, 4: 1 }
      3: { 6: 2, 4: 1, 2: 1 }
      4: { 5: 3, 1: 2, 2: 1 }
      5: { 1: 4, 6: 1, 4: 1 }
      6: { 2: 2, 4: 2, 5: 1 }
      7: { 1: 3, 3: 1 }
    source: functional harmony

  # The four Ethiopian qenit (ቅኝት).
  #
  # Mulatu Astatke, on what Ethio-jazz is: the four modes underneath, and the
  # world — Latin, American jazz, European — on top. That is the arrangement
  # this file makes possible, because the modes can now be the bottom.
  #
  # All four are pentatonic, which is the whole reason the spine had to stop
  # assuming seven degrees. The transitions are deliberately sparser than the
  # heptatonic ones: with five degrees there is no ii-V, and the motion these
  # modes actually make is stepwise around a strong tonic rather than
  # cadential. Weighted toward returning to 1, because in every recording of
  # these the tonic is where the phrase lands.
  #
  # Qualities lean on sus and triads rather than on the ninths the heptatonic
  # modes use: a pentatonic scale has no seventh degree to build a maj7 from,
  # and stacking one anyway is how a modal line stops sounding modal.

  tizita:
    # The best known of the four — the nostalgic one, major-pentatonic in shape.
    semitones: [0, 2, 4, 7, 9]
    qualities: { 1: maj, 2: sus, 3: min, 4: maj, 5: min }
    transitions:
      1: { 4: 3, 5: 2, 2: 2 }
      2: { 1: 3, 4: 2 }
      3: { 1: 2, 5: 2 }
      4: { 1: 4, 5: 2 }
      5: { 1: 4, 4: 1 }
    source: chromatone.center Ethiopian kignit — C D E G A

  tizita_minor:
    semitones: [0, 2, 3, 7, 9]
    qualities: { 1: min, 2: sus, 3: maj, 4: min, 5: min }
    transitions:
      1: { 4: 3, 5: 2, 3: 2 }
      2: { 1: 3, 4: 2 }
      3: { 1: 3, 5: 1 }
      4: { 1: 4, 5: 2 }
      5: { 1: 4, 4: 1 }
    source: chromatone.center Ethiopian kignit — C D Eb G A

  bati:
    semitones: [0, 2, 5, 7, 9]
    qualities: { 1: maj, 2: min, 3: sus, 4: maj, 5: min }
    transitions:
      1: { 3: 3, 4: 2, 2: 2 }
      2: { 1: 3, 3: 2 }
      3: { 1: 3, 4: 2 }
      4: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
      5: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
    source: chromatone.center Ethiopian kignit — C D F G A

  bati_minor:
    semitones: [0, 1, 5, 7, 9]
    qualities: { 1: min, 2: maj, 3: sus, 4: maj, 5: min }
    transitions:
      1: { 3: 3, 2: 2, 4: 2 }
      2: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
      3: { 1: 3, 4: 2 }
      4: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
      5: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
    source: chromatone.center Ethiopian kignit — C Db F G A

  ambassel:
    # DISAGREEMENT, recorded rather than resolved.
    #
    # chromatone.center gives Ambassel major as C D E G Ab -> [0, 2, 4, 7, 8].
    # A separate source describes it as C Db F G Ab -> [0, 1, 5, 7, 8], calling
    # the intervals a minor 2nd, major 3rd, major 2nd, minor 2nd and major 3rd,
    # and places it in the Gonder and Wollo regions.
    #
    # Those are different scales, not two spellings of one. Both are carried:
    # `ambassel` is the first, `ambassel_wollo` the second. Neither is guessed
    # at, and picking one silently would have made the engine confidently wrong
    # about a mode it cannot check.
    semitones: [0, 2, 4, 7, 8]
    qualities: { 1: maj, 2: sus, 3: min, 4: maj, 5: maj }
    transitions:
      1: { 5: 3, 4: 2, 2: 2 }
      2: { 1: 3, 5: 2 }
      3: { 1: 3, 5: 1 }
      4: { 1: 3, 5: 2 }
      5: { 1: 4, 4: 1 }
    source: chromatone.center Ethiopian kignit — C D E G Ab

  ambassel_wollo:
    semitones: [0, 1, 5, 7, 8]
    qualities: { 1: min, 2: maj, 3: sus, 4: min, 5: maj }
    transitions:
      1: { 3: 3, 2: 2, 5: 2 }
      2: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
      3: { 1: 3, 5: 2 }
      4: { 1: 3, 3: 1 }
      5: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
    source: second source, Gonder/Wollo — C Db F G Ab; see the note on `ambassel`

  anchihoye:
    # The most distinctive of the four and the least like anything in Western
    # practice: a minor 2nd, then a major 3rd, then a minor 2nd. The wide gap
    # in the middle is what makes it unmistakable.
    semitones: [0, 1, 5, 6, 9]
    qualities: { 1: min, 2: maj, 3: sus, 4: dim, 5: maj }
    transitions:
      1: { 3: 3, 2: 2, 5: 1 }
      2: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
      3: { 1: 3, 5: 1 }
      4: { 3: 2, 1: 2 }
      5: { 1: 4, 3: 1 }
    source: chromatone.center Ethiopian kignit — C Db F Gb A

`````

### dilla/data/pieces.yml

`````yaml
# The catalogue demo.wav plays: sixteen short pieces that are not each other.
#
# lib/pieces.rb lays a row's `bed` block over data/bed.yml and module Bed reads
# the result, so every number the bed has is a number a piece may set: its
# tempo, which oscillator families deal, which drum grids and which crate the
# kit comes out of, how loud and how treated the lead is, which console the
# master bus leaves through, and whether there are drums at all.
#
# `progression` names a row of CHORD_PROGRESSIONS in dilla.rb. All 413 of them
# voice; the five transcribed off Dilla records are here first, and the rest of
# the catalogue is drawn from the table's own writing.
#
#   ruby dilla.rb catalogue          all of it, joined into demo.wav
#   ruby dilla.rb piece fall_in_love out.wav
#   ruby dilla.rb pieces             the table, one line each
#
# A piece is repeatable because it is written here rather than drawn: the same
# name and the same RENDER_SEED give the same take.

# demo.wav: ninety seconds, not the whole catalogue.
#
# Thirty-one pieces is eighteen minutes and nobody listens to eighteen minutes
# of a demo. The showcase is ten of them at nine seconds each, ordered so no two
# neighbours share a tempo, a family, a drum bank or a console: a Rhodes vamp at
# 88, the operator's own ninths at 98, a Flying Lotus stagger at 72, four to the
# floor at 124, industrial at 138, footwork at 160, his own set at 166, then two
# ambient pieces with no kit at all and a half-time close. Everything the engine
# can be, inside a minute and a half.
#
# Nine seconds is two to four bars depending on the tempo, which is one statement
# of a loop. `ruby dilla.rb catalogue-full` renders all thirty-one at length.
showcase:
  seconds_each: 9
  crossfade_s: 0.7
  order:
    # The operator prefers demo2: industrial floor first (four_floor, detroit,
    # hate_rumble). Fall In Love and FlyLo follow.
    - four_floor
    - detroit
    - hate_rumble
    - fall_in_love
    - quartal_mediants
    - footwork
    - sandviken_hotell
    - still_water
    - two_moons
    - so_what

# What every piece starts from, before its own block.
#
# The lead is the change the operator asked for on 2026-09-16: at -7 dB playing
# one bar in four it was inaudible under the kit, which is not a quiet lead but
# an absent one. It plays three bars in four now, six dB louder, and its racks
# stack and freeze twice as often, because the layer is only worth having if it
# is heard.
defaults:
  # Measured on one piece, stem by stem: the kit peaked at -5.0 dB and sounded
  # 63.7% of the bar, while the lead peaked 6.0 dB under it and sounded 23.4%.
  # A layer present a quarter of the time and six decibels down is a layer
  # nobody hears, which is why an evening of work on the room it plays in
  # changed nothing anyone could hear. It plays nearly every bar now, and the
  # kit gives it the room.
  lead:
    gain_db: 4
    plays_odds: 0.95
    sit_out_bars: 32
    stack_odds: 0.3
    freeze_odds: 0.35
    gate_odds: 0.35
  catalogue: { min_chords: 4, max_chords: 8, crossfade_s: 1.0 }
  master_bus: { console: glue }

# The crates. `samples` names one file per voice under samples/drums.
kits:
  crate: &kit_crate
    { kick: kick.wav, snare: snare.wav, ghost: ghost.wav, hat: hat.wav, open_hat: open_hat.wav, clap: ind_clap.wav }
  industrial: &kit_industrial
    { kick: ind_kick.wav, snare: ind_clap.wav, ghost: ind_stab.wav, hat: ind_hat.wav, open_hat: open_hat.wav, clap: ind_clap.wav }

# The feels. Dilla time is the bed's own default and lives in bed.yml; these are
# the two that are not it.
feels:
  # Techno is the opposite instrument: nothing is pushed, nothing drags, and the
  # grid is the point. A swung four-to-the-floor is a shuffle, not a techno beat.
  rigid: &feel_rigid
    hat:   { swing: 0.0, shift: 0.0, drift: 0.0 }
    snare: { swing: 0.0, shift: 0.0, drift: 0.0 }
    kick:  { swing: 0.0, shift: 0.0, drift: 0.0 }
    ghost: { swing: 0.0, shift: 0.0, drift: 0.001 }
  # The abstract, West-coast side: hats swung, snare LATE, kick later still.
  #
  # Not Detroit, and the difference is one sign. Dilla time rushes the snare --
  # it arrives before the grid, against a kick that is swung and late, and that
  # collision is the whole feel. This drags the snare 33 ms behind instead, which
  # measured as a wider gap between the parts and sounded like trip-hop: a late
  # snare under a slow kick is the downtempo signature, not the Detroit one. It
  # is kept because it is a real feel and some material wants it; it is not what
  # a Slum Village piece should be given.
  experimental: &feel_experimental
    hat:   { swing: 0.14, shift: 0.006,  drift: 0.004 }
    snare: { swing: 0.10, shift: -0.018, drift: 0.005 }
    kick:  { swing: 0.22, shift: 0.024,  drift: 0.006 }
    ghost: { swing: 0.26, shift: 0.034,  drift: 0.008 }
  # Hardgroove: the kick is the clock and everything else rolls against it.
  #
  # The opposite construction to dilla time. There the hats are the rigid
  # reference and the kick is swung against them; here the kick is dead on the
  # floor -- it is the clock a room dances to and it cannot move -- and the
  # momentum comes from percussion rolling underneath it. The ghosts carry a
  # little swing and a little drift so the roll breathes rather than machine-guns,
  # and the hats sit fractionally late so the offbeat pulls against the kick
  # instead of sitting inside it. The snare is barely there, because in this music
  # the backbeat is not the event; the roll is.
  hardgroove: &feel_hardgroove
    hat:   { swing: 0.0,  shift: 0.004,  drift: 0.001 }
    snare: { swing: 0.0,  shift: 0.0,    drift: 0.001 }
    kick:  { swing: 0.0,  shift: 0.0,    drift: 0.0 }
    ghost: { swing: 0.08, shift: 0.006,  drift: 0.004 }
  # Hard triplet swing, hats included, which is the footwork and shuffle side.
  swung: &feel_swung
    hat:   { swing: 0.2,  shift: 0.0,    drift: 0.002 }
    snare: { swing: 0.22, shift: -0.008, drift: 0.003 }
    kick:  { swing: 0.24, shift: 0.010,  drift: 0.004 }
    ghost: { swing: 0.26, shift: 0.020,  drift: 0.005 }

# Silence is a gain, not a missing part: the kit still renders and still keys the
# sidechain, so the pads breathe on a pulse nobody hears.
no_drums: &no_drums { gain_db: -60 }

pieces:
  # ---- Dilla, transcribed ------------------------------------------------
  - name: fall_in_love
    progression: eb_minor_two_chord
    note: Slum Village, prod. J Dilla — the Gap Mangione vamp, Rhodes and nothing else in the way.
    bed:
      bpm: 88
      bars_per_chord: 4
      pad_families: [rhodes]
      pad_voice: rhodes_tine
      pad_racks: [wash]
      overtones: { partials: [2, 3, 4, 6], gain_db: -21 }
      lead: { plays_odds: 0.55, rack_names: [tape, ghost] }
      drums: { arrangement: { bank_order: [dilla], bars_per_shape: 4 }, samples: *kit_crate  }
      master_bus: { console: twelve_bit, crush_bits: 12, crush_mix: 0.24 }
      catalogue: { min_chords: 4, max_chords: 4, crossfade_s: 1.0 }

  - name: time_donut
    progression: maj7_minor_cycle
    note: Donuts — Time (The Donut of the Heart), the Ab cycle at ninths.
    bed:
      bpm: 92
      pad_families: [rhodes, prophet]
      pad_voice: e_piano
      pad_racks: [shimmer]
      hocket_odds: 0.45
      overtones: { partials: [2, 3, 5], gain_db: -23 }
      lead: { rack_names: [weather, octave] }
      drums: { arrangement: { bank_order: [dilla], bars_per_shape: 8 }, samples: *kit_crate  }
      catalogue: { min_chords: 8, max_chords: 8, crossfade_s: 1.0 }

  - name: get_dis_money
    progression: pedal_e_descent
    note: Slum Village, prod. J Dilla — Herbie's slash loop over an E pedal.
    bed:
      bpm: 82
      pad_families: [prophet]
      pad_voice: prophet_pad
      pad_racks: [wash]
      reverse_odds: 0.3
      overtones: { partials: [2, 3, 4, 5, 6], gain_db: -19 }
      lead: { gain_db: 1, rack_names: [ring, inharmonic] }
      drums: { arrangement: { bank_order: [dilla], bars_per_shape: 4 }, samples: *kit_crate  }
      master_bus: { console: twelve_bit }

  - name: climax
    progression: e_major_third_rise
    note: Slum Village — Climax. Major, which in this catalogue is the exception.
    bed:
      bpm: 94
      pad_families: [moog]
      pad_voice: poly_lead
      pad_racks: [shimmer]
      min_attack_s: 0.25
      overtones: { partials: [2, 4, 6, 8], gain_db: -22 }
      lead: { plays_odds: 0.85, rack_names: [octave, weather] }
      drums: { arrangement: { bank_order: [dilla, dilla, flylo], bars_per_shape: 4 }, samples: *kit_crate  }
      catalogue: { min_chords: 8, max_chords: 8, crossfade_s: 1.0 }

  - name: so_what
    progression: dorian_two_chord_modal
    note: Jamal's two chords by way of Miles, at half time, where the space is the arrangement.
    bed:
      bpm: 74
      bars_per_chord: 4
      pad_families: [moog]
      pad_voice: prophet_pad
      pad_racks: [wash]
      min_attack_s: 0.9
      overtones: { partials: [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8], gain_db: -18 }
      lead: { plays_odds: 0.5, gain_db: -3, rack_names: [ghost, tape] }
      drums: { arrangement: { bank_order: [dilla], bars_per_shape: 8 }, samples: *kit_crate, gain_db: -9  }
      catalogue: { min_chords: 4, max_chords: 4, crossfade_s: 1.0 }

  # ---- The abstract side -------------------------------------------------
  - name: quartal_mediants
    progression: flylo_quartal_mediants
    bed:
      bpm: 72
      pad_families: [prophet]
      pad_voice: surreal_wash
      pad_racks: [shimmer]
      hocket_odds: 0.6
      reverse_odds: 0.28
      overtones: { partials: [3, 5, 7], gain_db: -20 }
      lead: { plays_odds: 0.9, gain_db: 1, rack_names: [inharmonic, ring, ghost] }
      drums: { arrangement: { bank_order: [flylo, broken], bars_per_shape: 4 }, samples: *kit_crate }
      master_bus: { console: blown, width: 1.18 }
      catalogue: { min_chords: 4, max_chords: 6, crossfade_s: 1.0 }

  - name: hexatonic_shiver
    progression: hexatonic_pole_shiver
    note: Two triads a major third apart with one tone in common — the horror-film hinge, played warm.
    bed:
      bpm: 66
      pad_families: [prophet, moog]
      pad_voice: surreal_wash
      pad_racks: [shimmer]
      overtones: { partials: [2, 3, 5, 6], gain_db: -19 }
      lead: { rack_names: [ghost, inharmonic] }
      drums: { arrangement: { bank_order: [flylo], bars_per_shape: 8 }, samples: *kit_crate, gain_db: -8 }
      master_bus: { console: air }

  - name: lament_ground
    progression: lament_ground
    note: The descending tetrachord every century has used for grief, over a boom-bap kit.
    bed:
      bpm: 86
      pad_families: [rhodes, prophet]
      pad_voice: rhodes_tine
      pad_racks: [wash]

  # ---- The archive ------------------------------------------------------
  #
  # Fifteen progressions read out of the operator's own Ableton sets, 2008 to
  # 2024, by `dilla.rb import-als`. Each carries its chords here rather than
  # naming a row of CHORD_PROGRESSIONS, because they are his and belong to no
  # table. The tempo is the set's own. The instrument is not: those sets ran
  # chipsounds, Analog Lab, MrRay73, DX7 V and a Sonitex STX-1260, and this
  # engine synthesises everything it plays, so what comes back is the writing.

  - name: dnb_ninths
    chords: ["Fm9", "Ebm9", "Ab9", "Dbmaj9", "C7#9", "Fm9", "Bbm9", "Dbmaj7"]

    bed:

      overtones: { partials: [2, 3, 4, 6], gain_db: -20 }
`````

### dilla/dilla.rb

`````ruby
#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true
#
# Dilla — unified audio engine
# Synthesis, analog pads, vocal mixes (v7–v11), stem rack, demux, MIDI electronium.
#
# Usage: ruby dilla.rb help

# lib/music_gems must load — and bootstrap! must run — before anything else
# requires a gem this Gemfile.lock pins (json 2.19.1, yaml/psych, ostruct):
# whichever code activates a gem name first wins for the whole process, and an
# unconstrained `require "json"`/`require "yaml"` below would activate
# whatever version ships as a Ruby default gem (e.g. json 2.20.0 on 3.4.9),
# so bootstrap!'s own `require "bundler/setup"` then conflicts and silently
# disables coltrane/midilib/wavefile/head_music for the rest of the process
# (bootstrap! rescues LoadError). Real invocations run plain `ruby dilla.rb`,
# not `bundle exec`, so this ordering is the only thing that pins it correctly.
# Before anything reads a file. The engine's own sources carry UTF-8 — em dashes
# and Norwegian vowels in comments and track names — and 37 File.read/readlines
# sites across lib/ ask for no encoding, so they inherit the locale's. Under a C
# or POSIX locale that is US-ASCII, and the first thing to read a source file
# raises: `env -i ruby dilla.rb help` died at lib/ledger.rb:228 building the knob
# table, before printing a word of help.
#
# It never bit interactively because a login shell exports a UTF-8 LANG. It bites
# anything that does not: cron, a minimal deploy shell, an agent's non-login
# invocation. One assignment here rather than an encoding: argument on all 37,
# which is also how RAILS/gates/runner.rb solved the identical problem — see
# OPENBSD/lib/utf8.rb and the comment above its require.
Encoding.default_external = Encoding::UTF_8

require_relative "lib/music_gems"
DillaMusicGems.bootstrap!
# The one definition of which files the engine is made of. Required this early
# because it has no dependencies and defines the engine's own corpus.
require_relative "lib/engine_sources"
# Every file the engine is made of: dilla.rb and lib/*.rb. `wiring_check`,
# `debug`, `where`, provenance and the stream's restart-on-edit all mean the
# engine, and a method body reading this constant must not find it undefined
# because the method sits above the line that sets it.
ENGINE_SOURCES = DillaSources.all

# Everything the caller set before dilla touched the environment.
#
# force_env! overwrites unconditionally, so a style table always beat the
# command line: `SONITEX=heavy ruby dilla.rb ...` rendered donuts_warm,
# because DILLA_STYLE_DEFAULTS force both SONITEX and SONITEX_PRESET and ran
# after the caller's value was already in place. That is true of every knob
# those tables name, not just this one -- the documented environment
# variables were advisory at best.
#
# Captured before any require can mutate ENV. force_env! consults it and
# records the skip in config_provenance, so `print_config_provenance` shows
# which values the caller pinned and which a style chose.
#
# The stream re-execs itself when this file's mtime changes, and exec inherits
# the whole environment — including everything apply_best_defaults! and the
# style tables had already written into it. So after one restart the child's
# "user pins" contained TRACK/PROGRESSION=pedal_e_descent, values no user ever
# typed, and force_env! then refused to let any track's own progression
# overwrite them. Asking for slum_village_players_documented rendered its name
# and its 91 BPM over pedal_e_descent's chords, and no amount of restarting fixed
# it because each restart re-laundered the same defaults.
#
# The restart therefore declares the real pin set, and only those keys count as
# pinned in the child. Absent the declaration (a normal command line) every
# environment variable present at load is a pin, as before.
USER_PINNED_ENV = begin
  declared = ENV["DILLA_USER_PINNED_KEYS"]
  captured = ENV.to_h
  captured.delete("DILLA_USER_PINNED_KEYS")
  if declared.nil?
    captured
  else
    keys = declared.split(",")
    captured.select { |k, _| keys.include?(k) }
  end
end
`````
